arxiv-2301-10653.title: Polar magneto-optic Kerr and Faraday effects in finite periodic 𝒫 ​ 𝒯 \mathcal{P}\mathcal{T} -symmetric systems
arxiv-2301-10653.creator: Antonio Perez-Garrido, Peng Guo, Vladimir Gasparian, Esther Jódar
arxiv-2301-10653.description: Abstract We discuss the anomalous behavior of the Faraday (transmission) and polar Kerr (reflection) rotation angles of the propagating light, in finite periodic parity-time ( 𝒫 ​ 𝒯 \mathcal{P}\mathcal{T} ) symmetric structures, consisting of N N cells. The unit cell potential is two complex δ \delta -potentials placed on both boundaries of the ordinary dielectric slab.

arxiv-2505-09525.title: An Asymptotically Optimal Approximation Algorithm for Multiobjective Submodular Maximization at Scale
arxiv-2505-09525.creator: Fabian Spaeh, Atsushi Miyauchi
arxiv-2505-09525.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Fabian Spaeh, Atsushi Miyauchi. Maximizing a single submodular set function subject to a cardinality constraint is a well-studied and central topic in combinatorial optimization. However, finding a set that maximizes multiple functions at the same time is much less understood, even though it is a formulation which naturally occurs in robust maximization or problems with fairness considerations such as fair influence maximization or fair allocation.

arxiv-2602-16594.title: Decentralized and Fully Onboard: Range-Aided Cooperative Localization and Navigation on Micro Aerial Vehicles
arxiv-2602-16594.creator: Abhishek Goudar, Angela P. Schoellig
arxiv-2602-16594.description: Abstract Controlling a team of robots in a coordinated manner is challenging because centralized approaches (where all computation is performed on a central machine) scale poorly, and globally referenced external localization systems may not always be available. In this work, we consider the problem of range-aided decentralized localization and formation control.

pmc-11387480.title: Highly sensitive detection of kojic acid in food samples using fluorescent carbon dots derived from pomegranate peel
pmc-11387480.creator: Omnia H Hassan, Ahmed S Saad, Mohsen Ghali
pmc-11387480.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Kojic acid (KA) has gained significant attention due to its widespread use in the food and cosmetics industries. However, concerns about its potential carcinogenic effects have heightened the need for sensitive detection methods. This study introduces a fluorescence-based optical sensor for the quantification of KA in food samples, utilizing fluorescent carbon dots (CDs) synthesized from pomegranate peel via a hydrothermal method.

pmc-11481317.title: Identification of sex-specific markers using genome re-sequencing in the blunt snout bream (Megalobrama amblycephala)

pmc-11481317.description: BackgroundThe blunt snout bream (Megalobrama amblycephala) is an important economic freshwater fish in China with tender flesh and high nutritional value. With the cultivation of superior new varieties and the expansion of breeding scale, it becomes imperative to employ sex-control technology to cultivate monosexual populations of M. amblycephala, thereby preventing the deterioration of desirable traits.

pmc-11565587.title: Generating pregnant patient biological profiles by deconvoluting clinical records with electronic health record foundation models
pmc-11565587.creator: David Seong, Samson Mataraso, Camilo Espinosa, Eloise Berson, S Momsen Reincke, Lei Xue, Chloe Kashiwagi, Yeasul Kim, Chi-Hung Shu, Philip Chung, Marc Ghanem, Feng Xie, Ronald J Wong, Martin S Angst, Brice Gaudilliere, Gary M Shaw, David K Stevenson, Nima Aghaeepour
pmc-11565587.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Translational biology posits a strong bi-directional link between clinical phenotypes and a patient’s biological profile. By leveraging this bi-directional link, we can efficiently deconvolute pre-existing clinical information into biological profiles. However, traditional computational tools are limited in their ability to resolve this link because of the relatively small sizes of paired clinical–biological datasets for training and the high dimensionality/sparsity of tabular clinical data.

pmc-11925741.title: Racismos y salud mental en jóvenes indígenas residentes en la Zona Metropolitana de Oaxaca, México

pmc-11925741.description: RESUMENLas poblaciones indígenas presentan altas prevalencias de trastornos mentales y limitado acceso a servicios de salud mental. El objetivo del estudio fue analizar las trayectorias de atención a trastornos mentales de jóvenes indígenas residentes en la Zona Metropolitana de Oaxaca, México.

pmc-12375103.title: NLSTseg: A Pixel-level Lung Cancer Dataset Based on NLST LDCT Images
pmc-12375103.creator: Kun-Hui Chen, Yi-Hui Lin, Shawn Wu, Nai-Wen Shih, Hsing-Chen Meng, Yen-Yu Lin, Chun-Rong Huang, Jing-Wen Huang
pmc-12375103.description: Low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) is the most effective tools for early detection of lung cancer. With advancements in artificial intelligence, various Computer-Aided Diagnosis (CAD) systems are now supported in clinical practice. For radiologists dealing with a huge volume of CT scans, CAD systems are helpful. However, the development of these systems depends on precisely annotated datasets, which are currently limited.

pmc-12509726.title: Isavuconazole: Need for therapeutic drug monitoring and CYP polymorphism testing
pmc-12509726.creator: Rajeev Soman, Sanraksha Mayya, Rahul Doshi, Inderdeep Singh, Sushrut Ganpule
pmc-12509726.description: In this patient of invasive sinusitis due to Rhizopus arrhizus, Therapeutic drug monitoring (TDM) showed a high trough level (88mg/L) of isavuconazole on standard doses. Genotyping revealed CYP3A5∗3/∗3 polymorphism which indicated poor metabolism of isavuconazole. Switching to posaconazole was attempted but there was intolerance to posaconazole.

pmc-12976661.title: Discovering PETases: An Interlink Between Engineering Enzymes and Microbiomes
pmc-12976661.creator: Diego Javier Jiménez, Alexandre Soares Rosado
pmc-12976661.description: Polyethylene terephthalate (PET), an abundant synthetic polyester, is the only plastic that has been enzymatically recycled at an industrial scale. Over the last decades, research efforts have focused on screening and engineering PET‐degrading hydrolases (PETases), aiming to identify variants that can operate efficiently in both environmental and industrial settings.

pmc-13089474.title: Development and Validation of a Predictive Model for Postoperative Nausea and Vomiting in Thyroid Cancer Patients: A Retrospective Case-Control Study
pmc-13089474.creator: Fangfang Li, Zifeng Li, Shengmei Wu, Zuyang Xi, Yuyan Tan
pmc-13089474.description: BackgroundThyroid cancer is the most prevalent endocrine malignancy, with surgical intervention being the primary treatment modality. Postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV) are common complications following thyroid surgery, significantly impacts patient recovery. Consequently, this study analyzed the risk factors for PONV in patients with thyroid cancer post-surgery and developed a predictive model.

pmc-13202046.title: Enhancing parental health knowledge through digital knowledge mobilisation tools: a randomised controlled trial and qualitative study
